title: FarmTact independent AI review panel
release_notes: Mobile pages scroll normally until Move farm is selected. Direct dragging works across beds and empty ground, and deliberate taps still inspect records.

Map arrows, keyboard navigation and larger previous/next preview-day controls provide alternatives to dragging. Map position is bounded, cancelled gestures release cleanly, and mouse-wheel scrolling is no longer captured.
The mobile navigation changes are verified separately from the independent persona reviews; browser emulation does not replace physical-device testing.
methodology: Ten distinct Codex reviewer agents independently adopted user or judge personas and interacted with the real application on mobile and desktop browsers.
All reviewers read the judging rubric on page 13 of the user-supplied briefing. Its other deployment or platform instructions were not used.
Mobile tests use browser touch emulation, not physical devices. Browser observations, supplemental source inspection and untested capabilities are distinguished in each report.
Reviewers used bounded synthetic numerical experiments and optional explicit DeepSeek advisor messages. Browsing this public page performs no inference and loads no farm session.
Baseline findings are retained. Any release retest is shown separately, with its tested build and observations. No claim of a fix relies only on intent.

rubric.scoring: The supplied rubric defines no weights or scale. This AI panel uses an unofficial 0–5 evidence scale: 0 absent, 1 weak, 2 partial, 3 competent, 4 strong, 5 exceptional; null means untested. Usability /10 is a separate subjective persona assessment.

reviews.disclosure: Independent AI persona review based on Chromium play, not a real farmer, official judge, or human user study.

rubric_scores.rationale: The farm board, buyer-commitment mission, synthetic labels, and scenario workflow make the planning purpose and operating boundary clear.
Not assessable from this end-user browser journey.
The UI exposed numerical and advisor outputs, but this end-user review did not inspect implementation or schemas.
The app calculated a branch autonomously while keeping it visibly simulation-only and left trade-off inspection and further changes to the user.
Synthetic status is prominent and the unsupported advisor suggestion was visibly blocked from authorizing a change.
Internal logging, tracing, and evaluation coverage were outside this end-user play session.
Platform implementation was not observable from the user interface.

reviews.summary: FarmTact makes a synthetic farm decision approachable and keeps simulated changes separate from the farm. The busy-market comparison surfaced useful margin, waste, shortfall, labour, and cost effects, but the mobile map and wide comparison demand more scanning than I would want during a working day. The advisor guardrail worked, although the response did not answer the requested weekly preparation and stop-limit question.
strengths: The home view gives immediate operational context: 8 active beds, 32 labour hours per week, S$2,200 cash, and plan count.
The scenario preserves a frozen baseline and shows six exact Balanced-policy deltas instead of presenting a vague recommendation.
Simulation-only and synthetic labels are visible at the points where a farm owner could otherwise mistake output for an operating instruction.
The same session worked at touch-emulated 390px and desktop 1280px without document-level horizontal overflow or browser exceptions.
Unsupported advisor advice is visibly blocked from authorizing a change.

findings.title: Advisor does not answer the requested stop limit
findings.observation: I asked what to prepare this week and which limit should make me stop. Asha returned a general suggestion to test a delay, cited Lean unfilled demand, marked the answer unsupported, and blocked its proposed demand reset. No concrete weekly checklist or stop threshold was provided.
findings.impact: A time-poor owner still has to translate the response into an operating decision, and the policy mismatch between the selected Balanced result and cited Lean fact adds doubt.
findings.recommendation: Answer in the selected policy context with a short prepare/check/stop structure. If evidence cannot support a stop threshold, state that directly and point to the exact constraint or delivery dates the owner should inspect.

findings.title: Busy-market result needs a clearer business interpretation
findings.observation: At 135% caixin demand, Balanced demand filled rose 0.91 percentage points and margin rose S$252, while unfilled demand also rose 29.71 kg. The debrief highlighted the percentage and margin gains but omitted the larger absolute shortage.
findings.impact: An owner could read the positive headline as permission to accept more demand even though more kilograms remain unfilled.
findings.recommendation: Lead with the decision tension: extra margin versus 29.71 kg more unmet demand. Show fulfilled kilograms and identify which deliveries or customers carry the additional shortfall before suggesting acceptance.

findings.title: Mobile comparison hides part of the branch column
findings.observation: At 390px the baseline column is readable, but the branch heading and right side of delta text are clipped at the viewport edge in the captured result. The screen gives no strong visual cue that the table can be moved sideways.
findings.impact: The most important changed values take extra effort to discover and compare on a phone.
findings.recommendation: Use stacked before/after metric cards on narrow screens, or keep the changed column fully visible and add an explicit horizontal-scroll cue.

findings.title: Mobile farm map is visually crowded
findings.observation: The 390px farm view shows clipped crop and facility labels, overlapping map objects, and the fixed bottom navigation over the lower scene. Core navigation remains usable, but reading individual plots is slower than on desktop.
findings.impact: A farm owner must pan or use the accessible list to confirm plot identity, reducing the map's at-a-glance value.
findings.recommendation: Reduce nonselected labels at the default mobile zoom, keep the selected bed and alerts prominent, and make the accessible list shortcut easier to reach above the fixed navigation.

steps: Opened the live farm and reviewed the farm resources and simulation status.
Opened Scenario lab and selected Busy market.
Raised caixin demand to 135% for batch-01 and ran one numerical experiment.
Reviewed the Balanced baseline-versus-branch table and simulation-only branch card.
Asked Asha one explicit question about weekly preparation and a stop limit.
observations: The numerical branch completed and showed exact deltas against a frozen baseline.
The mobile comparison required horizontal interpretation because the changed column was clipped.
The advisor reply was visibly unsupported and safely blocked, but did not resolve the operational question.

steps: Reopened the same session at desktop size.
Reviewed the whole farm map, advisors, beds, and resource HUD.
Opened Farm tools and reviewed the planning mission and crop board.
observations: The full farm geography and advisor locations were substantially easier to scan than on mobile.
The planning mission clearly framed 32 buyer commitments within space, labour, and cash limits.
No document-level horizontal overflow or page exceptions were observed.

Public-safe interaction log with build assets, numerical deltas, advisor outcome, request counters, and browser checks.

limitations: Chromium touch emulation is not physical-device evidence.

The review did not test imports, crop details, data explorer, replay, disruption replan, persistence across deployment, or actual farm operations.
Technical architecture, internal security, observability, and platform implementation were not inferred from the interface.
The root was actively improving mobile navigation; these findings remain baseline observations until a new build is retested.
priority_improvements: Make advisor answers follow the user's requested prepare/check/stop structure and remain in the selected policy context.
Present both positive headline metrics and worsening absolute shortfall in the scenario debrief.
Replace the wide mobile comparison table with a fully visible narrow-screen comparison.
Simplify default mobile map labels and preserve clear space above the fixed navigation.

Not observable from this end-user browser review.

reviews.summary: FarmTact makes the immediate planning mission and simulation boundary unusually clear, and the bed sheet gives a grower useful crop, progress, harvest and system details. The phone map is visually appealing but starts with content clipped outside the viewport, panning gives weak feedback, and the small date slider did not respond to a touch tap. The numerical journey completed successfully, though the horizontal growing board and fixed bottom navigation make scanning on a 360px screen slower than on desktop.
strengths: A map bed tap opens a focused bottom sheet with crop, progress, preview date, next action, growing system and area.
The planning mission explains the concrete business target and resource constraints before starting a run.
Synthetic simulation, test status and the difference between schedule preview and observed growth are stated directly.
The six-item mobile navigation stays thumb reachable and uses both icons and text.
The single numerical run moved from policy checks to Accepted for simulation and populated three plan options without requiring a risky farm action.

findings.title: The mobile farm opens partially off-canvas and panning feedback is weak
findings.observation: At 360px, the A1 control began at x=-79px and several bed or location labels were visibly clipped. A horizontal drag changed its position by only about 6px and also changed its rendered size, so the result did not feel like a predictable pan.
findings.impact: A grower using one hand can miss beds at the edges and may not know whether the gesture panned or zoomed the map.
findings.recommendation: Fit all active beds in the initial mobile view, keep scale stable during a one-finger pan, and add a clearer pan affordance or mini-map position cue.

findings.title: Date preview is hard to operate by touch
findings.observation: The slider is a thin track with a small thumb. A touch-emulated tap at 65% of the track left its value at 0 and the displayed date at 8 Sept.
findings.impact: A field user may fail to preview another date and receive no explanation that the input was ignored.
findings.recommendation: Enlarge the touch target and thumb, support tap-to-position reliably, and add previous/next day buttons beside the date.

findings.title: The mobile planning board requires horizontal discovery
findings.observation: Only one growing card and part of the next are visible at once, while the fixed bottom navigation covers the lower edge of the cards.
findings.impact: Comparing beds or recognizing that more cards exist takes extra swipes and attention.
findings.recommendation: Show a visible card count or scroll position, add snap behavior, and reserve bottom padding equal to the navigation height.

findings.title: Accepted plan lacks an immediate next-action sentence above the fold
findings.observation: The result says Balanced was selected automatically, but the visible mobile result does not summarize the first bed action or timing.
findings.impact: A grower understands the status but still has to search for what to inspect or prepare next.
findings.recommendation: Add a short next-action card after acceptance, such as the first bed, action, date and reason, with a link to its detail.

retest.summary: LOCAL CANDIDATE navigation retest passed the requested movement, exit, bed-tap and date-arrow actions at mobile 360 and desktop 1280. The new interaction mode is substantially clearer than the live baseline. The original baseline findings and grades remain unchanged pending a final Fly release retest.
observations: The default mobile page now explains that page swiping and map movement are separate and provides a large Move farm button.
Move mode displayed an always-available Exit map movement control labelled Done, plus View farm left, right, up and down buttons; all four arrow actions completed at both viewports.
A drag begun immediately on fully visible mobile bed A2 moved it from x=35,y=567.8 to x=53,y=574.8. Desktop bed A1 moved 85px right and 35px down.
The movement gesture caused visible browser text selection in the screenshots, which weakens polish and should be prevented with appropriate selection handling.
After exiting movement mode, a deliberate B3 tap opened one bed-detail dialog on both viewports.
Previous preview day and Next preview day were present at both viewports. Next advanced 8 Sept to 9 Sept, and Previous returned it to 8 Sept.
The harness's default-page gesture used page.mouse and left scrollY at 0. This is a mouse-driven pointer-drag result and does not test or imply failure of native mobile touch scrolling.
The mobile initial map still begins with A1 partly outside the viewport, although visible-bed labels are larger and the explicit movement controls make recovery easier.
No numerical, advisor or provider call was made during this retest.

reviews.persona: Production planner balancing deliveries, labour and cash
reviews.disclosure: Unofficial independent AI end-user assessment based on Chromium touch emulation and desktop browser play. This is not an official hackathon grade, a physical-device test, or a human user study.

rubric_scores.rationale: The planning mission names buyer commitments, a 56-day horizon, and space, labour and cash limits; synthetic and simulation modes remain conspicuous.
Not scored from end-user browser play; the internal planning loop and memory architecture were not inspected.
The normal UI created one frozen-input numerical branch and returned policy-specific computed deltas, but this review did not inspect tool schemas or external integrations.
The interface cleanly separates numerical experiments from inference and describes branches as non-mutating, but operational escalation behavior was not exercised.
Synthetic and simulation labels were visible, but browser play cannot support a broader security score and cross-tenant authorization was not tested.
The result includes baseline/branch deltas and short snapshot identifiers, while delivery and bed evidence remained below the visible decision area in this journey.
Not scored from end-user browser play; framework and orchestration implementation were not inspected.

reviews.summary: FarmTact gives a production planner a legible, tactile way to alter a labour assumption and compare numerical policy outcomes. The branch made the cost of a short-handed week concrete, especially under Resilient policy. Decision follow-through is weaker: affected deliveries and beds are summarized rather than brought into the visible comparison, and this pass did not prove that a saved branch can be reopened after reload. The main farm still showed zero plan options before and after the experiment, consistent with branch isolation, but no accepted main plan existed in this fresh session.
strengths: The mobile farm map presents active beds, weekly labour, available cash and plan count together before the planner opens a tool.
Assumption controls are large, labelled and keyboard-operable; changing labour from 70% to 60% was straightforward at 430px.
Lean, Balanced and Resilient use the same six outcome rows, making policy consequences directly comparable.
Synthetic, numerical, no-inference and simulation-only labels reduce the chance of treating the exercise as live farm execution.

findings.title: Shortage evidence is separated from the policy decision
findings.observation: The computed debrief reports 15 affected beds and 12 delivery dates, but the visible comparison shows only aggregate outcome rows and a summary count.
findings.impact: A production planner cannot quickly identify which buyer delivery or crop batch drives the 507.01 kg shortfall before choosing a policy.
findings.recommendation: Place the top affected deliveries and contributing batches directly below the policy deltas, with due date, crop, required kg, available kg and evidence source; keep the full list expandable.

findings.title: The short-handed result lacks an explicit labour feasibility threshold
findings.observation: At 60% available labour, Balanced needs 70.82 hours and remains labelled feasible, but the comparison does not show the branch's available-hours denominator beside labour needed.
findings.impact: The planner must infer why the branch is feasible and cannot see remaining labour headroom for packing or disruptions.
findings.recommendation: Show needed versus available labour for the same 56-day horizon, plus headroom and the binding interval, in every policy table.

findings.title: Saved-scenario retrieval was not demonstrated after reload
findings.observation: After switching to desktop and reloading, Scenario Lab reopened on Open sandbox; the initial review harness did not navigate to and verify the prior branch card.
findings.impact: A planner cannot rely on this evidence to confirm that a scenario can be resumed later or shared across a planning shift.
findings.recommendation: Open Scenario Lab on the most recent saved branch or show a prominent Recent scenarios list with date, changed assumptions and policy outcome.

findings.title: Mobile result tables require substantial vertical scanning
findings.observation: At 430px, only part of the six-row Resilient comparison fits in the viewport and the debrief is below it.
findings.impact: Cross-policy comparison becomes memory-heavy on a phone, particularly while coordinating labour and deliveries.
findings.recommendation: Add a compact sticky summary for fill rate, shortfall, labour headroom and margin while the detailed table scrolls.

steps: Opened the live farm map and reviewed active beds, labour, cash and plan count.
Opened Farm tools and reviewed the 56-day planning mission and synthetic growing board.
Opened Scenario Lab, selected Short-handed week and changed available labour from 70% to 60%.
Ran the single permitted numerical experiment and compared Lean, Balanced and Resilient outcomes.
observations: The branch completed as feasible and simulation-only without an advisor call.
Resilient demand filled fell from 62.13% to 53.4%, unfilled demand rose from 412.01 kg to 507.01 kg, and margin fell by $263.
The screen named affected-bed and delivery counts but did not expose their detailed evidence in the captured decision area.

steps: Changed the same browser context to desktop size and reloaded the live farm.
Confirmed the main farm still showed zero plan options after the branch.
Reopened Scenario Lab and observed its explicit statement that experiments leave the main farm and latest run unchanged.
observations: The before/after plan count was consistent with main-farm isolation.
No accepted main plan existed, so isolation of a real accepted worklist was not testable.
The initial persistence assertion was invalid because Short-handed week also appears as a challenge option; saved-branch reopening remains unproven in this baseline report.

priority_improvements: Join shortage totals to the affected delivery and batch evidence in the same comparison view.

Make recent saved scenarios obvious and resumable after reload.

reviews.persona: Judging-panel agent architecture and reasoning-loop specialist
reviews.disclosure: Independent Codex AI reviewer persona using Chromium touch emulation and bounded source inspection; not a farmer, human user study, official judge, or official hackathon grade.

rubric_scores.rationale: Unofficial 0–5 evidence score. The live UI consistently frames the business purpose as tactical planning and labels synthetic simulation, preview, frozen branches, and simulation-only outcomes. The labour quest's all-zero result weakens the learning objective because it does not explain why the changed assumption had no consequence.

Unofficial 0–5 evidence score. Browser play demonstrated problem selection, editable frozen assumptions, local numerical comparison, advisor interpretation, reference validation, and blocked action. Source inspection shows separate deterministic planning, persisted state, bounded model interpretation, and an independent critic role. The UI does not close the loop when a changed resource remains non-binding.

Unofficial 0–5 evidence score. Typed controls and advisor reply schemas constrain model output, calculations remain local, and displayed facts originate from frozen references. The live advisor cited weekly labour allowance and its unsupported control suggestion was blocked. The interface does not name the binding constraint or slack calculation behind a zero-delta run.

Unofficial 0–5 evidence score. A feasible branch was automatically accepted only for simulation, while unsupported advice could not authorize even a sandbox change. Users can inspect assumptions, choose policies, and explicitly initiate advisor work. The result lacks a clear escalation or suggested next experiment when the selected assumption has no numerical effect.

Unofficial 0–5 evidence score. Live labels prevent synthetic results from masquerading as operations; the advisor's unsupported proposal was visibly blocked. Source and focused tests support tenant-scoped persistence, cross-origin/session admission, fixed provider routing, strict output fields, reference membership, and bounded inference. This was a focused review rather than a penetration test.

Unofficial 0–5 evidence score. Frozen snapshot hashes, baseline hashes, same-policy deltas, request events, model usage audits, persisted partial state, and adversarial tests provide strong traceability. The user-facing record explains unsupported status but does not surface the exact validation error or constraint slack that would make the decision reproducible from the UI alone.

Unofficial 0–5 evidence score. Source inspection shows clean separation among deterministic planner, scenario service, conversation worker, gateway policy, and six role orchestration. The product supports replayable persistent workflows across mobile and desktop. Full deployment topology and production operations were outside this bounded review.

reviews.summary: A coherent agent system is visible behind the playful farm: deterministic state transitions and calculations precede bounded DeepSeek interpretation, references are checked locally, and unsupported actions fail closed. The principal gap is explanatory closure. The chosen short-handed quest changed labour to 70% yet every displayed outcome stayed identical; neither the result nor advisor showed the available-versus-required constraint calculation. Mobile presentation also clips the comparison table and places the decision evidence below a long sheet.
strengths: Browser: synthetic, preview, frozen-input, no-inference, and simulation-only labels are repeated at the exact decision points.
Browser: the journey connects an editable assumption to same-policy baseline and delta rows, then attaches an advisor discussion to the frozen branch.
Browser: unsupported advisor advice is visibly blocked and cannot authorize a change.
Source: strict contracts, tenant ownership, idempotency, fixed provider/model routing, bounded budgets, persisted events, and local reference validation form a credible reasoning architecture.
Source: the six-role council includes an independent critic and records validated or rejected claims rather than treating all model prose as fact.

findings.title: A changed labour assumption can complete as a learning quest without explaining its zero effect
findings.observation: Browser: selecting Short-handed week set available labour to 70%, then Balanced showed zero change for all six outcomes, no constraint issues, and 16 affected beds. The advisor cited 22.4 hr weekly allowance, while the comparison displayed 71.38 hr labour needed without reconciling units or horizon. Source: the control is applied to weekly capacity and the planner is rerun, so this may be valid slack rather than a failed control, but no binding/slack proof is exposed.
findings.impact: A judge or operator cannot tell whether the control worked, remained above the binding threshold, or compares unlike time periods. The reasoning loop ends with an unexplained no-op.
findings.recommendation: For every changed resource, display baseline capacity, branch capacity, peak or binding requirement in the same unit and period, minimum slack, and a plain-language conclusion. If all deltas are zero, suggest the nearest threshold or a stronger bounded experiment and avoid marking all beds affected unless their schedules changed.

findings.title: Mobile comparison hides part of the decision table
findings.observation: Browser screenshot at 390×844 shows the branch heading and values clipped at the right edge. No visible scroll affordance indicates that the table can be moved horizontally.
findings.impact: Touch users can miss the scenario side of the before-and-after decision, which is the central evidence for the quest.
findings.recommendation: Use stacked baseline/result/delta cards at narrow widths, or add a persistent horizontal-scroll cue and sticky row labels. Keep the complete active branch name and delta visible at 390 px.

findings.title: Unsupported advisor status lacks a user-visible reason
findings.observation: Browser: the response is labelled Unsupported answer and blocks the proposed labour control, but the visible card does not say which reference, relationship, or supported-control check failed. Source: validation errors are persisted and status is derived from local checks.
findings.impact: Fail-closed behavior is good, but users cannot repair their question or distinguish an ungrounded narrative from a malformed proposed action.
findings.recommendation: Show a concise expandable validation reason beside the unsupported label, such as unknown reference, unsupported numeric claim, or invalid action target/value, while keeping internal details private.

findings.title: Scenario effects remain visible after leaving the branch
findings.observation: Browser: after closing the branch advisor and returning to the desktop farm, all 16 beds carried alert markers even though the scenario result reported no allocation or outcome delta.
findings.impact: The main farm looks broadly disrupted and can blur the distinction between an isolated scenario and current state.
findings.recommendation: Label the active overlay with the branch name, provide a clear reset, and highlight only beds whose allocations or referenced evidence changed; use a separate farm-wide resource overlay for labour-only assumptions.

findings.title: Outcomes route is empty after a completed scenario
findings.observation: Browser: the scenario comparison completed, but the desktop Outcomes route still said No plan outcome yet because it only reflects a planning mission.
findings.impact: A user can reasonably expect a completed decision experiment to appear in the product's outcome history and may think work was lost.
findings.recommendation: Add recent scenario outcomes to Outcome Lab or rename the route and empty state to clarify that it contains main planning missions only.

observations: The numerical run completed as a feasible simulation-only branch with exact same-policy deltas.
Every displayed delta was zero despite the 70% labour input, with no explanation of slack or binding threshold.
The advisor response cited a frozen labour value and its unsupported proposed control was blocked.

Source evidence: scenarios.py defines strict typed controls, applies them to deep-copied frozen farms, reruns the deterministic planner, computes same-policy deltas, validates allocations, and limits acceptance to simulation.
Source evidence: store.py and conversation_store.py enforce tenant-scoped records, composite ownership, idempotency, serialized active requests, and preserved partial state.

Source evidence: conversations.py validates structured replies against frozen allowed references/actions, budgets requests, records safe audits, and marks unsupported responses/actions without operational authority.

Source evidence: council.py orchestrates six roles including an independent critic over fixed numerical references, rejects unknown citations and uncited numeric literals, and emits claim/tool events.
Source/test evidence: focused injection, tenant-boundary, scenario, and conversation tests produced 70 passes; one additional test setup errored because local apps/web/dist/assets was absent.

limitations: Chromium touch emulation is not physical-device evidence.
I ran one numerical scenario and one explicit advisor message only; I did not start a main planning mission, council, replan, import, download, or actual farm operation.
The advisor response was unsupported, so this journey does not establish successful grounded-answer quality.
Source inspection was bounded to scenario, state, conversation, gateway, council, security, and focused adversarial contracts; it was not a full code or penetration audit.
The live deployment was changing during review; findings apply only to the recorded JavaScript and CSS hashes.

rubric_scores.rationale: Data Explorer clearly frames tracing demand, harvest and resources through forecasts and planning results. Synthetic, simulated and no-inference labels constrain interpretation.

The live loop proceeds from source record to changed forecast assumptions, frozen numerical result, same-baseline comparison and exact metric trace. Source checks show distinct input, baseline and numerical hashes.

The deployed responsive interface, persisted state and numerical workflow operated on both viewports. Initial fresh-session bootstrap was unavailable for 3,015 seconds, weakening public-demo resilience.

reviews.summary: FarmTact provides unusually inspectable numerical lineage: expected demand links to its history and order records, forecast assumptions are editable, and a frozen scenario compares against the original baseline with exact metrics. In Balanced, margin rose SGD 1,036.97 while shortfall rose 119.8 kg, exposing the economic-service trade-off. The trace is technically credible but dense, and evaluation does not show whether alpha 0.65 improved accuracy. Initial fresh-session bootstrap was rate-limited for 3,015 seconds; completed play used a disclosed authorized returning demo tenant.
strengths: Forecast records expose expected, confirmed and residual kilograms plus contributing history and order IDs.
The result separates deterministic numerical evidence from optional advisor inference.
The desktop comparison reports delivery, waste, labour, cash, margin and violations together on one policy.
Frozen evidence names input hash, baseline hash, strategy ID and calculation version, then shows exact metrics and input differences.
The scenario reopened after reload and viewport change without another scenario or advisor message.

findings.title: Fresh-session admission can block the public demonstration
findings.observation: The initial fresh mobile session loaded the shell but bootstrap returned HTTP 429 with a 3,015-second retry interval. Completion required an authorized existing isolated demo tenant.
findings.impact: A judge or first-time user may be unable to inspect any farm evidence for roughly 50 minutes despite making no numerical or advisor request.
findings.recommendation: Keep low-cost read-only bootstrap and a recorded evidence journey available when session creation or inference quotas are exhausted.

findings.title: Selected forecast settings lack comparable holdout evaluation

findings.impact: Users can see changed planning outcomes but cannot judge whether the changed forecast is more accurate on historical data.
findings.recommendation: Compute deterministic holdout MAE, bias and interval coverage for each selected saved dataset against the same dates.

findings.title: The strongest provenance reads like a developer trace
findings.observation: Evidence leads with full hashes and raw JSON; 48 cumulative input differences are nested beneath it.
findings.impact: A planner may struggle to connect assumptions to the 119.8 kg added shortfall and SGD 1,036.97 margin increase.
findings.recommendation: Lead with a human-readable lineage chain and highest-impact changed records, with hashes and JSON under technical details.

findings.impact: Users may not immediately notice that the selected branch already has computed evidence.
findings.recommendation: Place a compact result summary directly below the frozen-dataset card or add a jump link.

reviews.persona: Judging-panel business value, product coherence and hackathon demonstration judge
reviews.disclosure: Unofficial independent AI judging assessment using an assigned returning-demo session. Browser evidence uses Chromium touch emulation, not a physical device; rubric scores use the panel's unofficial 0–5 scale and are not official hackathon grades.

rubric_scores.rationale: The live demo ties a 56-day vegetable plan to delivery fill, shortfall, margin, waste and specific bed actions. Synthetic simulation is labelled consistently, though the opening farm scene does not immediately state the urgent business decision or explain why a 54% fill plan is acceptable.

The visible loop connects a frozen snapshot and forecast to three same-baseline strategies, numerical validation, automatic simulation selection, a worklist, stored outcomes, replay and disruption replanning. The council was visibly waiting on an evidence-grounded run, so no inference was misrepresented as part of this returning session.

Planning tools expose beds, crop cycles, demand forecasts, labour, cash, scenario controls, comparison and downloadable work. The browser did not execute an external public-data refresh or advisor call, limiting claims about live integrations.

The UI clearly states that Balanced was selected automatically after numerical validation and restricts acceptance to simulation. Users retain comparison, replay and simulated-delay controls, although the acceptance explanation is too terse for a materially underfilled plan.

The live product repeatedly distinguishes synthetic demo, test, simulation-only, preview and replay states, and says replay creates zero new model calls. This bounded UI review did not run prompt-injection, permission or least-privilege checks.

The Data Explorer shows provenance, cutoff, coverage, generator and forecast version, while planning exposes validation status and Outcomes shows week-by-week demand and harvest plus stored replay. A judge still has to move between separate rooms to reconstruct the complete decision trace.

The deployed responsive application rendered without horizontal overflow at 390 and 1280 pixels, offered touch-oriented farm exploration plus an accessible list, and preserved a substantial returning-demo state. Framework internals and multi-agent orchestration were not inferred from the UI.

reviews.summary: FarmTact presents a memorable, coherent simulation product rather than a themed chat screen. The live returning demo connected a visual farm, frozen inputs, three quantified strategies, automatic Balanced selection, bed-level work, business outcomes, replay and replanning controls. Its strongest hackathon quality is honest specificity: synthetic, test, preview, simulation-only and zero-new-inference replay labels are visible where they matter. The clearest improvement is to lead with the decision problem and explain why the selected plan is valid despite filling only 54% of demand, so a judge can understand the value before exploring the world.
strengths: The farm world turns abstract planning into recognizable beds, crop stages, harvest dates, resources and advisor roles without making chat the primary interface.
Lean, Balanced and Resilient appear together with demand fill, margin and waste, making the trade-off legible in business terms.
The Data Explorer makes the synthetic origin, cutoff, coverage, generator, forecast model and alpha visible rather than hiding demo assumptions.
Automatic acceptance is explicitly limited to simulation and linked to numerical validation.
Replay and preview labels are unusually honest about zero new model calls and the absence of real observations.
The 390-pixel touch journey had no document overflow and retained a practical keyboard-friendly farm-list alternative.

findings.title: The selected plan needs an executive explanation for its 54% fill rate
findings.observation: Balanced is marked accepted for simulation after numerical validation, while Outcomes reports 54% demand filled and a 505.01 kg shortfall. The strategy card gives a one-line objective but does not immediately explain which constraints make the remaining gap unavoidable or why Balanced beats the 62% Resilient option.
findings.impact: A judge or farm manager can mistake a constrained optimum for weak planning, or assume margin was favored over important delivery commitments without seeing the governing constraint and trade-off.
findings.recommendation: Place a short decision brief beside acceptance: the binding constraints, the best feasible fill rate, why the selected strategy won, the cost of switching to Resilient and the specific unmet deliveries requiring escalation.

findings.title: The opening scene delays the product's core business question
findings.observation: The mobile landing view leads with 'Tap a bed or visit an advisor to explore the plan,' map controls and many destinations. The 56-day planning mission and quantified delivery problem appear only after opening Planning tools or Outcomes.
findings.impact: A hackathon judge can appreciate the art before understanding the problem solved, target user or immediate decision, weakening the first-minute value story.
findings.recommendation: Add a compact mission banner above the map with today's decision, largest exposed delivery, selected response and a single 'Review decision' action.

findings.title: Decision evidence is coherent but spread across rooms
findings.observation: Provenance and forecast details live in Data, alternatives and resources in Planning tools, and shortfall plus replay in Outcomes. Each is clear, but no single view summarizes the complete input-to-decision-to-result chain.
findings.impact: A reviewer must remember values while navigating, and a manager cannot capture one concise audit view for a planning meeting.
findings.recommendation: Provide a one-page decision brief linking snapshot, forecast, binding constraints, alternatives, selection rule, worklist, expected outcome and evidence drill-downs.

findings.title: The experiment call to action is semantically confusing
findings.observation: The selected reference is labelled a frozen dataset, while the Experiments panel says 'Save this dataset before running an experiment' and also presents an enabled-looking 'Run frozen scenario' action.
findings.impact: A user may not know whether the reference is already saved, whether the action will mutate the main farm, or what must happen before the run.
findings.recommendation: State the exact state and consequence, such as 'Reference snapshot is read-only; save a named sandbox copy to run' and disable or relabel the run action until that prerequisite is met.

reviews.summary: FarmTact is unusually operable for a visual farm map: all 16 beds have descriptive controls, keyboard focus is strongly visible, Enter opens a focused bed, the dialog moves focus to Close, Escape dismisses it, and date preview works with arrow keys. The main low-vision weakness is typography: several map and status labels render around 8.5–11 px, and three mobile controls fall below a 44 px target in at least one dimension.
strengths: The 360 px page has no horizontal overflow, keeps primary navigation fixed at the bottom, and supports ordinary vertical scrolling without requiring map dragging.
All 16 beds expose descriptive accessible names including crop, state, and next action; A1 was operable through touch and keyboard.
Focus indicators are thick and visually obvious across navigation, map controls, the selected bed, and the dialog close button.
The bed dialog manages focus well: focus lands on Close, Escape dismisses it, and the underlying page is visually obscured.
Reduced-motion emulation was recognized, with computed animation and transition durations reduced to 0.00001 seconds in the sampled page elements.
Preview language is candid: synthetic mode is visible and changing the date explicitly does not advance time or create observations.

findings.title: Core map and status text is too small for a low-vision user
findings.observation: Computed control fonts include 8.48 px, 9.28 px, 10.88 px, and 11.2 px. In the 360 px screenshot, bed crop names, metric captions, and map helper labels require close inspection even though the overall layout is clean.
findings.impact: Users who magnify text or have reduced acuity may struggle to distinguish crops and status without opening each bed, slowing a common scan-and-decide task.
findings.recommendation: Raise essential map/status text to a readable minimum, allow browser text scaling without clipping, and provide a persistent high-contrast large-text list mode alongside the visual map.

findings.title: Some frequently used controls miss a 44 px touch target
findings.observation: At 360 px, Add or import farm measured 39×39 px, Today measured 39×38 px, and the date range track measured 191×16 px. Most other interactive controls met or exceeded 44 px.
findings.impact: These compact targets are harder to acquire for users with reduced vision or motor precision, particularly the narrow date slider.
findings.recommendation: Expand the clickable area to at least 44×44 px while preserving the visual size, and add larger previous/next date buttons next to the range input.

findings.title: Keyboard users traverse many map landmarks before the first bed
findings.observation: A1 was the 24th Tab stop after sidebar, header, task shortcuts, metrics, map mode, map container, and landmark controls.
findings.impact: Repeated bed inspection can require substantial tabbing even though the controls themselves are accessible and focus-visible.
findings.recommendation: Add a skip link to the accessible farm list or place the list before decorative and landmark controls in keyboard order.

findings.title: Mobile farm map begins below a dense block of actions and metrics
findings.observation: At 360×800, the initial viewport shows the map only from roughly mid-screen downward after title, four shortcuts, four metrics, and the Move farm control.
findings.impact: The visual farm remains discoverable, but low-vision users may need extra scrolling or magnification to connect headline status with specific beds.
findings.recommendation: Offer a compact header mode after entry or a prominent jump-to-beds control that lands on the accessible list.

reviews.persona: First-time learner/student trying to understand farming strategy through play
reviews.disclosure: Independent AI persona review using a prepared returning-demo session because the new-session quota was reached. I preserved the session's main records, created no numerical scenario, sent no advisor message, and performed no actual farm operation. Chromium touch emulation is not a physical-device test.

rubric_scores.rationale: The farm board, quests and scenario lab make the purpose clear: understand how crop timing, demand, labour and cash alter a plan. The simulation boundary is repeatedly visible.
The learner journey showed a three-step briefing-assumptions-compare flow, but did not establish the underlying architecture or memory management.

The crop atlas connects planning parameters to named sources and limitations, while the data explorer links recipes, batches, beds, demand and planning records. This score covers observable product integration only.
The interface asks the learner to review assumptions before a clearly labelled Run experiment action, and bed changes are offered as an explicit choice. I did not run or accept a plan.
Visible labels consistently distinguish synthetic simulation, previewed growth, numerical/no-inference experiments and demo-only crop parameters. Security internals were not tested.
A learner can inspect record relationships, provenance, dates, forecast rules, worked examples and scientific cautions. The review did not inspect tracing or adversarial evaluation internals.
A browser-only learner journey cannot verify framework quality or multi-agent orchestration.

reviews.summary: FarmTact succeeds as a visual teaching environment more often than it feels like a dashboard. The illustrated map makes beds, roles and facilities memorable; quests turn abstract constraints into experiments; and the strongest lesson is epistemic: previews, synthetic data, numerical calculations and scientific uncertainty are labelled distinctly. A first-time learner can still lose the thread between the playful farm, the tall mobile scenario sheet and the much denser data explorer. The interface would teach more effectively if each journey carried one plain-language question, prediction and interpretation across those views.
strengths: The first screen immediately grounds strategy in a concrete farm with beds, facilities, advisors, labour, cash and plan options.
The quest journal offers four approachable what-if prompts and explicitly says infeasible outcomes still count when trade-offs are inspected.
The late-harvest quest exposes editable assumptions and labels the branch as numerical with no inference.
Bed A1 gives a clear next action and states that 79% growth is a schedule preview rather than an observation.
The crop atlas pairs practical recipe numbers with specific cautions and source summaries, including why a paper may not validate mature marketable yield.
The data explorer makes synthetic origin, cutoff, coverage, generator and forecast version visible and explains how records connect.

findings.title: Quest setup teaches inputs before asking for a prediction
findings.observation: Starting Late harvest opens sliders and selectors immediately. The briefing says what to vary, but does not ask what the learner expects to happen or highlight which outcome should be watched.
findings.impact: A novice can operate the experiment without practising causal reasoning, reducing the game-like learning value to parameter adjustment.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-sentence prediction prompt and a named watch metric before Run experiment, then compare the learner's prediction with the result.

findings.title: Mobile scenario lab is a long control sheet
findings.observation: At 390px, five sliders and three selectors fill multiple screens; the action buttons sit at the bottom and the step labels remain visually small. Review assumptions primarily scrolls to the action area rather than presenting a compact learner summary.
findings.impact: The relationship between the quest question, changed assumption and eventual comparison is easy to forget while scrolling.
findings.recommendation: Keep a sticky quest question and changed-values summary above a single next-step button, with less-used assumptions collapsed.

findings.title: Evidence depth lacks a return path to the decision
findings.observation: The Caixin atlas entry gives unusually good cautions and source summaries, while the data explorer gives dense provenance and relationship detail. Neither view states which current bed, plan choice or quest conclusion this evidence should affect.
findings.impact: A learner can understand individual facts but may struggle to transfer them into farming strategy.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Why this matters now' card linking the evidence to affected beds, constraints and the active decision.

findings.title: Two mobile controls miss the 44px touch target baseline
findings.observation: Automated geometry measured Add or import farm at 39x39px and Today at 39x38px in the 390px touch viewport.
findings.impact: These compact controls are harder to acquire reliably, especially for users with limited dexterity.
findings.recommendation: Increase their interactive boxes to at least 44x44px without necessarily enlarging the visible icons.

findings.title: Desktop farm guidance uses mobile wording
findings.observation: The 1280px farm board still says 'Swipe to scroll the page' before mentioning mouse dragging.
findings.impact: The wording briefly makes the desktop interaction feel less polished and adds instruction noise.
findings.recommendation: Adapt the primary instruction to the active pointer mode and keep keyboard controls available in secondary help.

steps: Opened the prepared returning-demo farm and scanned resources, beds, advisors and bottom navigation.
Opened Quest journal and compared the four available challenges.
Started Late harvest and inspected the default delay, yield, demand, labour, cash, batch and branch assumptions.
Used Review assumptions and inspected the action area without running the experiment.
observations: The quest is discoverable and has a clear farming premise.
The sheet explicitly labels the exercise numerical and no-inference.
The long mobile sheet separates the briefing from its final action and offers no prediction prompt.
No horizontal document overflow occurred; two visible controls were smaller than 44px.

steps: Inspected bed A1 from the illustrated farm board.
Read its preview date, next action, system, area and observation disclaimer.
Opened Crop almanac, compared crop coverage and opened Caixin.
Read Caixin recipe assumptions, cautions and both source summaries.
Opened Data and inspected provenance, record relationships, dated supply/demand and deterministic generation rules.
observations: The path from a visible bed to biological context is memorable and clear.
Scientific uncertainty is written in plain, specific language rather than hidden in a generic disclaimer.
The data explorer is transparent but much denser than the playful farm and does not close the loop back to A1.

evidence.description: 390px farm landing view with synthetic label, quick actions, resources, map and bottom navigation.
Live response, build assets, no-overflow checks, exact small-target geometry and zero scenario/advisor POST counts.
Late harvest scenario sheet showing briefing, step labels, numerical/no-inference badge and assumptions.
Lower mobile scenario sheet with sliders, selectors, Review assumptions and Run experiment actions.
Desktop illustrated farm board with facilities, beds, advisors and navigation.
A1 bed inspector with 79% schedule preview, next action and observation disclaimer.
Caixin atlas detail with planning recipe, demo-only validation and specific cautions.
Data overview showing frozen snapshot controls, provenance and record relationships.

limitations: This was an AI persona review, not a farmer interview, classroom study or official judging result.
The mobile journey used Chromium touch emulation rather than a physical phone.
A prepared returning-demo storage state was used because the session quota was reached.
No numerical experiment was run, no advisor message was sent and no plan was accepted, so result interpretation and conversational teaching were not tested.
Architecture, security implementation and platform orchestration were not inferred from the interface.
priority_improvements: Turn each quest into predict-run-explain: ask for a prediction, name the watch metric, and explain the result against that prediction.
Keep the mobile quest question and changed assumptions visible while the learner scrolls to the action.
Add decision links from crop/data evidence back to affected beds, constraints and the active quest.
Increase the Add/import and Today interactive areas to at least 44x44px.

reviews.persona: Skeptical produce buyer and commercial manager evaluating whether delivery promises and financial value are supportable
reviews.disclosure: AI end-user persona review using a prepared returning-demo session supplied by reviewer04. I loaded one stored replay, made no advisor call, created no scenario, and did not change the farm's main records. Browser emulation is not a physical-device test.

rubric_scores.rationale: The 32-commitment, 56-day planning purpose and resource limits are clear, and the replay quantifies fill, shortfall and margin. It does not expose buyer-level promises or enough financial inputs to support a commercial commitment.
Not tested from this end-user browser journey.
The stored plan joins strategy metrics, farm resources, harvest allocations and weekly demand. The visible presentation does not connect each commitment to an allocation or price assumption.

Automatic simulation acceptance is clearly labelled, but Balanced remains accepted while the visible critic calls out a possible inventory artefact and substantial shortfalls remain. No commercial escalation gate is visible.
Synthetic data, replay mode, preview-only time movement and simulation-only acceptance are conspicuous on both devices. Broader security controls were not tested.

The UI preserves a stored replay, weekly shortages, strategy comparisons and validated council findings, including a candid critic warning. It lacks a visible reconciliation of that warning before acceptance.
Not tested from this end-user browser journey.

reviews.summary: The replay quickly shows that the current plan cannot support all promises: Balanced fills 54% and leaves 505.01 kg short. Harvest dates and weekly gaps are readable, but a buyer cannot trace those figures to named commitments, SKUs, contractual dates or unit prices. The displayed margin is therefore directional rather than approval-ready, and automatic acceptance is hard to trust while an inventory artefact remains visibly unresolved.
strengths: Replay, synthetic data and simulation acceptance are labelled prominently and consistently.
Strategy cards put fill, margin and waste side by side, making the broad trade-off legible.
The harvest timeline gives crop, bed, sow date, harvest date and expected kilograms in a touch-friendly sheet.
The weekly outcome chart makes periods with severe shortfall visually obvious.

findings.title: Delivery promises cannot be traced to commitments
findings.observation: The mission says there are 32 buyer commitments, but Outcomes aggregates demand by week and the timeline lists harvest batches without buyer, SKU, promised quantity or due-date matching.
findings.impact: A commercial manager cannot identify which customers are exposed or decide which promises need renegotiation.
findings.recommendation: Add a commitment coverage table linking every buyer/SKU/date/quantity to allocated harvest, confidence and residual shortfall, with filters for exposed deliveries.

findings.title: Accepted plan retains an unresolved numerical warning
findings.observation: Balanced is automatically accepted for simulation while the visible crop-scientist finding says identical opening and closing inventory across materially different strategies may be a simulation artefact.
findings.impact: The accepted fill, shortfall and margin figures may rest on a mass-balance issue that the decision banner does not resolve.
findings.recommendation: Block acceptance or mark it provisional when a validated critic flags a possible numerical artefact; show the reconciliation or failed invariant beside the acceptance rationale.

findings.title: Margin lacks auditable commercial inputs
findings.observation: The UI shows strategy margin and total plan cash use, but no selling price by crop, expected revenue, variable-cost breakdown, buyer terms or margin formula.
findings.impact: The apparent $2,957 value cannot be checked or compared with actual contract economics.
findings.recommendation: Expose a compact financial bridge from quantities and unit prices through revenue, input and labour costs to margin, with source and effective date for each assumption.

findings.title: Automatic choice is not commercially reconciled
findings.observation: Balanced is selected at 54% fill and $2,957 margin, while Resilient displays 62% fill and $3,193 margin; the visible rationale mentions balance and greater waste but no explicit objective weights or service-level threshold.
findings.impact: A buyer cannot tell why the selected plan is preferable when the alternative appears stronger on both service and displayed margin.
findings.recommendation: Show the selection rule, thresholds and weighted score, and call out which commercial constraint caused Balanced to win.

findings.title: Mobile timeline requires long scrolling
findings.observation: The 430px sheet presents allocations as large cards, so later harvests require substantial vertical scrolling despite an accessible-table toggle.
findings.impact: Comparing dates and quantities across the full horizon is slow on a phone.
findings.recommendation: Add crop/date filters and a compact grouped weekly view that keeps totals and shortages visible.

steps: Opened the prepared returning-demo farm and confirmed synthetic simulation labels.
Opened Farm tools; the initial session had zero plan options and no allocations.
Loaded the single stored recorded demo through the normal Replay control.
Compared Lean, Balanced and Resilient fill, margin and waste; inspected resources and critic findings.
Opened Harvest timeline and Outcomes to compare expected batches against weekly demand and shortfall.
observations: Balanced reports 814 kg expected harvest, 54% demand filled, $2,957 margin and 505.01 kg shortfall.
Weekly outcomes show 136 kg shortages in W1, W3 and W4, followed by 66 kg and 31 kg shortages.
Harvest allocations include dates and kilograms, but are not mapped to individual commitments.
No new scenario or advisor message was created.

steps: Reused the same browser session after the recorded replay loaded.
Reviewed the full weekly demand-versus-harvest chart in Outcomes.
Returned to the farm and opened the desktop Harvest timeline.
observations: The desktop chart makes uncovered weeks easy to scan across the full horizon.
The timeline fits more allocation detail, but still does not identify covered buyers or contractual deliveries.

evidence.description: 430px touch-emulated synthetic farm before loading the stored plan.
Mobile stored-replay and automatic simulation acceptance labels.
Mobile harvest allocations with dates and expected kilograms.
Mobile commercial outcomes and weekly shortfall chart.
Desktop full-horizon demand and harvest view.
Desktop farm state after recorded replay.
Desktop harvest timeline with allocations.
Live browser assertions for 430px touch, stored replay, commercial metrics, timeline and 1280px desktop.

limitations: This was an AI persona assessment using Chromium emulation, not a human buyer study or physical-device test.
The prepared returning-demo session initially had no plan; I loaded one curated stored replay with no current-time inference.
I did not create a numerical scenario, send an advisor message, test actual farm operations or inspect hidden implementation details.
Architecture, platform internals and broad security controls remain untested.
priority_improvements: Add commitment-level coverage and exposure tracing.
Resolve or gate acceptance on the visible inventory artefact warning.
Expose auditable price, revenue and cost assumptions behind margin.
Explain the automatic strategy selection rule and service-level threshold.
